raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Keeps the CSF-compressed routed-expert block scales of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local` compressed on the GPU when the NVFP4 MoE backend is B12X: -2.57 GiB of weights, which is +18.7% KV cache on one RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q and +2.4 GiB of free memory on DGX Spark. GSM8K is unchanged.

Builds on #64312, which decodes CSF scales at load. Loading the checkpoint from the Hub also needs #64739 (shards under `tensors/`).

## Claims

- Lossless: the resident scales expand to exactly the scales #64312 decodes. A real-shape layer (512 experts, TP1/TP2/TP4 shards) expands every expert's scales byte-equal, and the encoder reproduces the checkpoint's own `csf` streams.
- Memory: weights 72.08 to 69.51 GiB on both GPUs.
- Cost: median ITL -4.0% at c=1, +6.9% at c=4, +8.8% at c=8 on DGX Spark (MTP-3); +1.4% / +3.0% / +6.8% on RTX PRO 6000. This is a capacity trade, taken only for checkpoints that declare `weight_scale_encoding: csf`.
- Only B12X W4A4 keeps scales resident. Other backends, W4A16, `csf_32x2_v1` and a `b12x` without the CSF API keep #64312's decode at load.

## Validation

DGX Spark (GB10), one node, base then this PR, median busy SM clock 2515 MHz in both arms. Base is main plus #64739; the checkpoint is the Hub layout of revision `b9ce18a6`. KV is fixed at 8 GiB on unified memory, so the saving shows as free memory.

| | main | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| model loading (GiB) | 72.08 | 69.51 | -2.57 |
| MemAvailable when ready (GiB) | 30.24 | 32.67 | +2.42 |
| median ITL c=1 / c=4 / c=8 (ms) | 88.78 / 124.09 / 171.31 | 85.19 / 132.62 / 186.39 | -4.0% / +6.9% / +8.8% |
| GSM8K-256, 5-shot (%) | 97.7 | 98.0 | |
| server ready (min) | 8.9 | 10.0 | +1.2 |

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (enforced 300 W), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, both arms twice in the order base, PR, base, PR on one node:

| | base | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| model loading (GiB) | 72.06 / 72.05 | 69.49 / 69.49 | -2.57 |
| KV cache (tokens) | 381,513 / 381,513 | 452,900 / 452,900 | +18.7% |
| median ITL c=1 / c=4 / c=8 (ms), mean of 2 | 15.47 / 20.60 / 27.15 | 15.68 / 21.22 / 28.99 | +1.4% / +3.0% / +6.8% |
| GSM8K-256, 5-shot (%) | 96.5 / 97.3 | 97.3 / 97.3 | |

Disclaimers:
- The RTX PRO 6000 runs used this PR's previous head (a6b2e2c, stacked on #64312 before it merged). The port to main moved the encoder next to the decoders and changed how the MoE method reads the encoding; the B12X path is unchanged. That GPU was not available for a rerun.
- ITL rather than TPOT: with MTP the per-token TPOT moves with acceptance length (2.03 to 2.26 across these runs).
- The Spark c=1 gain is within run-to-run noise; main and this PR on two other nodes measured 89.65 and 88.53 ms.

Tests (DGX Spark, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-40941f2c4b` with this branch's Python files overlaid):

```text
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py                     # 48 passed
pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py               # the 2 new tests pass
pre-commit (commit hooks, incl. mypy)                    # passed
```

`test_b12x_resident_csf_scales_match_decoded_scales` checks all-expert expansion byte-equal to the decoded scales, output identical to the decoded-scale kernel at one token (micro kernel) eagerly and under CUDA graph replay with the scratch poisoned between replays, and within 0.25 at 64 tokens (the dynamic kernel sums experts with atomics and differs from itself by up to 0.125). It also checks that a reload raises.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local --served-model-name flashnext \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend b12x \
  --language-model-only --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":32}' \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 8G --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \
  --engram-config '{"disk_offload":true,"cpu_offload":false}'   # Spark
  # RTX PRO 6000: --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 instead of the last two lines
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model flashnext --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts $((8*C)) \
  --max-concurrency $C --ignore-eos --seed 0          # C = 1, 4, 8
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 256 --temperature 0 \
  --max-tokens 512 --use-chat-completions --model flashnext \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```
</details>

## Details

**Design.** `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` takes the layer's `weight_scale_encoding` (per layer for `modelopt_mixed`) and asks the NVFP4 MoE oracle whether the selected backend keeps `csf` scales (`nvfp4_backend_supports_csf_scales`). Today only B12X with NVFP4 activations does, when the installed b12x exposes `Nvfp4CsfWeights` (FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 does). `B12xExperts.process_weights_after_loading` re-encodes the rank's decoded scales, hands them to b12x as `CsfScalePlanes`, and drops the decoded scale params. b12x expands only the routed experts' scales per call into one zero-initialized scratch per layer shape that all layers share; layers run one at a time on one stream, which makes sharing safe. The scratch is allocated at load, so CUDA graphs capture fixed pointers.

**Why re-encode instead of keeping the checkpoint streams.** #64312 decodes the streams in the weight iterator, before TP slicing, and the gate and up projections are separate matrices. Re-encoding the rank's decoded slice needs no loader change and works for any TP size. The encoder picks each row's base the way `csf` checkpoints do, so it costs nothing in size; FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 ships no encoder to reuse.

This PR does not:
- keep `csf_32x2_v1` (GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local) or W4A16 expert scales resident, or load streams straight to the GPU; released b12x has no API for that yet.
- change any backend other than B12X.
- support expert parallelism (B12X is TP-only) or weight reloading for resident layers (`NotImplementedError`, because captured graphs read the first load's storage).

## AI assistance

Prepared with AI assistance (code, tests and the measurement harness); I reviewed every line and ran the tests and benchmarks above. Not a duplicate: open PRs matching "csf", "resident scales", "weight_scale_encoding" and "b12x" contain no such change.

nodes.body:
@stecasta  Nice, this is the part #64312 left open.

A question before I start anything: are you planning an MXFP4 follow-up? FlashInfer's b12x already accepts `Mxfp4CsfWeights` in `prepare_weights` (and the inline W4A8 path reads the compressed scales directly), but vLLM's B12X MXFP4 backend doesn't use it yet. The missing piece looks like an encoder from the rank's E8M0 scales into the canonical planes, the same re-encode idea as here. I sampled gpt-oss-120b's expert scales and only about 1.2–3.5% fall outside a base/base+1 window, so it would save roughly 75–80% of them (around 2.8 GB on gpt-oss-120b). We already keep MXFP4 scales compressed in our own serving setup, so I'd be happy to send it as a follow-up on top of this one if you're not planning it.

Since MXFP4 checkpoints have no `weight_scale_encoding` to opt in with, would you rather gate it on a flag or a config option?

Separately: since the resident path re-encodes the decoded scales, `csf_32x2_v1` layers (GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local) could probably take the same route instead of staying decoded. Is keying it on the encoding mostly about keeping the scope small?

@stecasta  I found a FlashInfer dispatch issue while investigating resident-scale overhead: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8053.

The tensor API used here builds `MoeDecodeQuery` without forwarding `weight_plan.nvfp4_inline_scales`. It therefore leaves the capability false and expands the scales before dynamic GEMM, even when the existing kernel can read the compressed planes inline. The canonical preparation API already forwards this field. The fix adds the missing argument; existing batch/geometry eligibility checks still decide which kernel to use. The scale encoding, stored payload and compression ratio are unchanged.

On one DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), I checked a synthetic NVFP4 W4A4 layer at this PR's Qwen TP1 geometry: E512, H2560, I640, top-10, BF16 I/O, SiLU. Before/after use identical compressed weights, with 0.5% outlier scale bytes. Cold-L2 CUDA-graph CUPTI timings, median of three alternating rounds of 40 samples:

| Tokens | Spread routes: expansion → inline | Routes repeated over 16 experts: expansion → inline |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | 1325.27 → 1093.64 µs | 334.99 → 305.73 µs |
| 16 | 2551.57 → 2123.81 µs | 352.27 → 325.42 µs |
| 32 | 5019.16 → 4166.72 µs | 379.87 → 328.30 µs |

The probe checks exact output against a predecoded control and confirms that inline execution leaves poisoned expansion scratch untouched. The touched FlashInfer test file passes all 16 cases; three new compressed-plan cases fail without the fix. The existing vLLM resident-scale TP1/TP2/TP4 integration/graph tests also pass. The linked PR includes the reproducer and environment.

These are isolated synthetic MoE results, without the full model, TP collectives or MTP. They suggest an avoidable source of CSF overhead, but do not establish a full-model speedup or explain the entire reported ITL regression. I do not have this NVFP4 checkpoint cached for a matching serving run.

Hi @aijanai, that's fair. Right now the only way back to decoding at load is a different `--moe-backend`, which also changes the kernel. I'll add `VLLM_B12X_MOE_CSF_RESIDENT_SCALES=0` to keep the scales decoded at load as in #64312, next to the existing `VLLM_B12X_MOE_FP4_FORCE_A16`.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
I have one comment: there is no way to switch it off ,like an option or an env-var. If something goes sour, there is no way to go back to the old code path

+def test_b12x_resident_csf_scales_match_decoded_scales(

+    set_random_seed(29)

+    w2 = torch.randint(

+    ).to(torch.uint8)

+    w13_scale, w2_scale = (
+        torch.randint(0x28, 0x48, (*w.shape[:2], w.shape[2] // 8), device="cuda")

+        .view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        for w in (w13, w2)
+    )
+    alpha = torch.full((num_experts,), 1 / 64, device="cuda")
+    input_scale = torch.ones(num_experts, device="cuda")
+    kernels = {}

+                alpha,
+                input_scale,
+                w2.clone(),
+                w2_scale,
+                alpha,
+                input_scale,
+                is_act_and_mul=True,
+                reorder_w13=csf_scales,
+            )
+            if csf_scales:
+                expected_scales = (prepared[1].clone(), prepared[5].clone())
+            quant_config = FusedMoEQuantConfig.make(
+                quant_dtype="nvfp4",
+                weight_dtype="nvfp4",
+                w1_scale=prepared[1],
+                w2_scale=prepared[5],
+                g1_alphas=prepared[2],
+                g2_alphas=prepared[6],
+                a1_gscale=1.0 / prepared[3],
+                a2_gscale=1.0 / prepared[7],
+            )
+            kernel = _make_b12x_moe_kernel(
+                torch.empty(0, hidden_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+                prepared[0],
+                prepared[4],
+                topk,
+                MoEActivation.SILU,
+                quant_config,
+                csf_scales=csf_scales,
+            )
+            kernels[csf_scales] = (kernel, prepared[0], prepared[4])
+
+        experts = kernels[True][0].fused_experts
+        assert isinstance(experts, B12xExperts)
+        csf = experts._prepared()
+        csf.nvfp4_csf.decode_all(csf.w1_blockscale, csf.w2_blockscale)
+        for expanded, expected in zip(
+            (csf.w1_blockscale, csf.w2_blockscale), expected_scales
+        ):
+            assert torch.equal(expanded.view(torch.uint8), expected.view(torch.uint8))
+        with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="reloading"):
+            experts.process_weights_after_loading(
+                SimpleNamespace(
+                    apply_router_weight_on_input=False, _b12x_prepared_experts=csf
+                )
+            )
+
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(
+            64, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        scores = torch.randn(64, num_experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        topk_weights, topk_ids, _ = fused_topk(hidden_states, scores, topk, False)
+
+        def apply(csf_scales: bool, tokens: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+            kernel, w1, w2 = kernels[csf_scales]
+            return kernel.apply(
+                hidden_states=hidden_states[:tokens],
+                w1=w1,
+                w2=w2,
+                topk_weights=topk_weights[:tokens],
+                topk_ids=topk_ids[:tokens],
+                activation=MoEActivation.SILU,
+                global_num_experts=num_experts,
+                expert_map=None,
+                apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+            )
+

+def encode_csf_scales(
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]:
+    """Encode `[experts, rows, cols]` E4M3 block scales as `csf` streams.
+
+    A row's base is the lowest one whose 16-value window holds the most of the
+    row's bytes, which minimizes exceptions. Returns each expert's
+    `nvfp4_csf_fixed` and `nvfp4_csf_exceptions` stream on the CPU.
+    """
+    _, rows, cols = scales.shape
+    fixed: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    exceptions: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    # Bounds the per-row histograms to about 100 MB.
+    chunk_experts = max(1, (1 << 22) // (rows * cols))
+    for chunk in scales.view(torch.uint8).split(chunk_experts):
+        n = chunk.shape[0]
+        raw = chunk.reshape(-1, cols).long()
+        # below[:, k] counts the row's bytes smaller than k.
+        below = torch.zeros(raw.shape[0], 257, dtype=torch.int32, device=raw.device)
+        below.scatter_add_(1, raw + 1, torch.ones_like(raw, dtype=torch.int32))
+        below = below.cumsum(1)
+        bases = (below[:, 16:] - below[:, :241]).argmax(1, keepdim=True)
+        codes = raw - bases
+        outliers = (codes < 0) | (codes > 15)
+        codes = codes.masked_fill(outliers, 0).to(torch.uint8)
+        packed = codes[:, 0::2] | (codes[:, 1::2] << 4)
+        slabs = (bases.to(torch.uint8), packed)
+        fixed.extend(torch.cat([t.reshape(n, rows // 16, -1) for t in slabs], 2).cpu())
+        outliers = outliers.view(n, -1)
+        expert, position = outliers.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
+        words = chunk.reshape(n, -1)[expert, position].long() << 24 | position
+        words = torch.from_numpy(words.cpu().numpy().astype(np.uint32))
+        exceptions.extend(words.split(outliers.sum(1).tolist()))
+    return tuple(fixed), tuple(exceptions)
+
+

     encodings: Iterable[str],
 ) -> Callable[[Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]], Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]]:

issue_comments.body:
@stecasta  Nice, this is the part #64312 left open.

A question before I start anything: are you planning an MXFP4 follow-up? FlashInfer's b12x already accepts `Mxfp4CsfWeights` in `prepare_weights` (and the inline W4A8 path reads the compressed scales directly), but vLLM's B12X MXFP4 backend doesn't use it yet. The missing piece looks like an encoder from the rank's E8M0 scales into the canonical planes, the same re-encode idea as here. I sampled gpt-oss-120b's expert scales and only about 1.2–3.5% fall outside a base/base+1 window, so it would save roughly 75–80% of them (around 2.8 GB on gpt-oss-120b). We already keep MXFP4 scales compressed in our own serving setup, so I'd be happy to send it as a follow-up on top of this one if you're not planning it.

Since MXFP4 checkpoints have no `weight_scale_encoding` to opt in with, would you rather gate it on a flag or a config option?

Separately: since the resident path re-encodes the decoded scales, `csf_32x2_v1` layers (GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local) could probably take the same route instead of staying decoded. Is keying it on the encoding mostly about keeping the scope small?

@stecasta  I found a FlashInfer dispatch issue while investigating resident-scale overhead: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8053.

The tensor API used here builds `MoeDecodeQuery` without forwarding `weight_plan.nvfp4_inline_scales`. It therefore leaves the capability false and expands the scales before dynamic GEMM, even when the existing kernel can read the compressed planes inline. The canonical preparation API already forwards this field. The fix adds the missing argument; existing batch/geometry eligibility checks still decide which kernel to use. The scale encoding, stored payload and compression ratio are unchanged.

On one DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), I checked a synthetic NVFP4 W4A4 layer at this PR's Qwen TP1 geometry: E512, H2560, I640, top-10, BF16 I/O, SiLU. Before/after use identical compressed weights, with 0.5% outlier scale bytes. Cold-L2 CUDA-graph CUPTI timings, median of three alternating rounds of 40 samples:

| Tokens | Spread routes: expansion → inline | Routes repeated over 16 experts: expansion → inline |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | 1325.27 → 1093.64 µs | 334.99 → 305.73 µs |
| 16 | 2551.57 → 2123.81 µs | 352.27 → 325.42 µs |
| 32 | 5019.16 → 4166.72 µs | 379.87 → 328.30 µs |

The probe checks exact output against a predecoded control and confirms that inline execution leaves poisoned expansion scratch untouched. The touched FlashInfer test file passes all 16 cases; three new compressed-plan cases fail without the fix. The existing vLLM resident-scale TP1/TP2/TP4 integration/graph tests also pass. The linked PR includes the reproducer and environment.

These are isolated synthetic MoE results, without the full model, TP collectives or MTP. They suggest an avoidable source of CSF overhead, but do not establish a full-model speedup or explain the entire reported ITL regression. I do not have this NVFP4 checkpoint cached for a matching serving run.
